# Tracing the Embargo Breach

## Visual analytics for VAST Challenge 2026 · Mini-Challenge 1

::: {.hero-lede}
The embargo held until [18:00]{.stamp}. The information didn't.
:::

TenantThread's merger announcement was supposed to remain under embargo until **6:00 PM on 5 June 2046**. Merger-related information appeared publicly on FleX before that release time.

This is a reconstruction of how the breach happened: who was involved, how communication behaviour changed, and whether the release was a planned leak or a system breakdown under pressure.

::: {.dossier-facts}
[Embargo · 18:00]{.fact} [Rounds · 22]{.fact} [Messages · 912]{.fact} [Public posts · 77]{.fact}
:::

:::

## Project Background
TenantThread is a property technology company involved in a sensitive merger with CivicLoom Realty Partners. The deal, codenamed **Project HarborCrest**, was under strict information embargo. At the same time, TenantThread was facing rising public pressure over its **Retention Optimizer** product and growing criticism from SaltWind Journal and social media users.

An automated compliance tool known as **The Judge** was introduced to prevent embargo breaches. However, during the crisis, embargoed merger information still appeared publicly before the official release time.

This project investigates the communication records from the two weeks leading up to the breach to understand what happened.

## Key Findings

::: {.findings}

::: {.finding}
[Public posts]{.label}
[77]{.value}

<p>Merger information appeared publicly on FleX before the 6:00 PM release.</p>
:::

::: {.finding}
[Anonymous posts]{.label}
[12]{.value}

<p>Anonymous posting appears only inside the breach window, never before.</p>
:::

::: {.finding}
[Control gap]{.label}
[Round 14]{.value}

<p>FleX posts begin to outrun the Judge-Agent's compliance warnings.</p>
:::

::: {.finding}
[Side-channel messages]{.label}
[359]{.value}

<p>Sensitive coordination moved into low-visibility side channels.</p>
:::
